q: I think it is very important to always look at a few key points, the raceline should be you point of reference, it is the ideal line and therefore where a car wants to be, another important thing to look at is the track lines, So i think when cars are already next to each other before braking (that is the fronttire infront of the rear tire of the other) the both drivers always need to leave enough room on the track. when they are not braking forcing off is when they push the other car with  all
answer: During braking it is a bit different. An important rules is no moving while braking. When cars start braking you stick with the natural line you should take in that corner, so no changing direction exept for the corner itsself ofcouse. / What counts as a dive bomb and when is it good or bad, first of all from now on the input is gonna be way more. You should look where other drivers brake and judge if they go too late, ill let you decide what is too late, kinda depends on the corner, you need to check if they would even make the corner if there was no collision. To have a valid divebomb they need to have atleast their front tre infront of the other drivers rear tire, if not it is probably gonna be a bad divebomb, dont set that in stone cause maybe another rule will disagree with that, but most of the time if you just put you tire a bit in there it is gonna be that drivers fault. / At the apex if someone sends a good divebomb or the drivers are already side by side, the outside driver needs to leave atleast enough room that the other driver keeps atleast 2 tires on the road. on the exit the inside driver again cant push a driver over the line with all tire, also i forgot to say that only counts if there is runoff next to the line, if there is gravel or grass next to the line it is if the driver has no more room and has to drive onto the gravel or grass. / When should a driver around the outside back out. When a driver does not have atleast their front tire infront the rear tire at the apex the inside driver is allowed to drive towards the line, if they are the need to leave enough room on the exit.

q: Q5. On a straight (no corner), is any move across into a car alongside always at fault? What about one move to defend vs moving twice?
answer: I hate crashes on the staight, you will probably see way more both at fault incidents on the straight. Defending last minute, that the driver infront has no time to react is the fault of the defender, defending twice is also not okey. If both cars drift towards eachother they are both at fault if it ends up being a crash, if both had clear room to avoid it and followed the direction of the track and racingline. On the straight you  are side by side if any point of the car is next to the other driver.

q: Q31. Should severity score the move (how late, how fast, how reckless) or what happened after (spins, lost places, cars off)? Or 50/50?
